title: A Strongly Subcubic Combinatorial Algorithm for Triangle Detection with Applications

predicted_errors.error_location: Section describing TRIANGLE-DETECTION-1 and its correctness proof
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The central subroutine BFS+ is never defined. The proof refers to 'Step 12 of the modified BFS procedure' and Figure 1, but the paper contains no pseudocode or specification of BFS+, so the main algorithm and its claimed O(m) per BFS and triangle-detection guarantee cannot be verified.

predicted_errors.error_location: Case 2.1 of the proof that BFS+(s) finds a triangle
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The proof claims that if exactly one triangle vertex a is on level 1 and b,c are on level 2, then assuming b is discovered before c, the triangle {a,b,c} is detected while scanning b's adjacency list. This does not follow for a standard BFS if b and c are discovered by different level-1 vertices before a is processed. In such a graph, parent(b) and parent(c) may be different, and scanning b and seeing c already visited does not identify the common neighbor a unless BFS+ performs extra pairwise adjacency checks; no such checks or their cost are specified. Thus the claimed O(m) running time and correctness are unsupported.

predicted_errors.error_location: Time analysis of TRIANGLE-DETECTION-1, Phase I
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The algorithm repeatedly uses the adjacency matrix for O(1) edge tests, but if the graph is given by adjacency lists with m edges, constructing that matrix costs O(n^2). For sparse graphs with m = o(n^{3/2}), O(n^2) dominates the claimed O(m^{2/3}n) bound, and similarly affects the claimed O(m^{4/3}) bound unless an O(m)-time edge-query structure is used. The paper does not address this preprocessing cost.

predicted_errors.error_location: Theorem 2 and proof of the O(m^{4/3}) bound
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper announces two variants, TRIANGLE-DETECTION-1 and TRIANGLE-DETECTION-2, but only TRIANGLE-DETECTION-1 is given. The proof of the O(m^{1/2}n) and O(m^{4/3}) bounds refers to TRIANGLE-DETECTION-2 with parameter x ~ n^{1/2}, but that algorithm is never formally specified.

The text defines T_3(m) as the time to find a triangle in a graph with m edges but evaluates it as T_3(n) for n segments, conflating vertices and edges. The intersection graph of n segments can have Theta(n^2) edges; substituting Theorem 2's O(m^{4/3}) bound then gives O(n^{8/3}), not the claimed O(n^{4/3}). The claimed O(n^{4/3}) runtime from replacing the BMM-based algorithm is therefore unsupported.
